items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: Rosja zajmuję Ukrainę. Co to oznacza dla Polski? Odcinamy całą pomoc dla Ukrainy. Zamykamy lotnisko w Rzeszowie. Ani palety, ani naboju. Tak, jak chce Konfederacja. Co dalej? Jasionka stoi pusta. Przez Polskę szło osiemdziesiąt procent zachodniej broni dla Ukrainy. Teraz nie idzie nic. Ukraiński żołnierz liczy naboje. Miesiąc szósty. Front pęka. Dziś mamy w Polsce milion Ukraińców. Chcieli mniej. Dostajemy drugą falę, kilka milionów uchodźców, w tym uśpieni rosyjscy agenci. Po roku Ukraina upada i mamy 1160 kilometrów granicy z Rosją i Białorusią. Najbardziej doświadczona armia współczesnej Europy, która od 4 lat uczy się zabijać dronami staje przeciwko nam. A wraz z nimi największy przemysł zbrojeniowy Europy. Duński wywiad policzył resztę. Po pół roku Rosja będzie gotowa na wojnę lokalną, a po dwóch - na regionalną. Oszczędzimy na cudzej wojnie. Zapłacimy za własną. A co zrobi Konfederacja w obliczu takiej sytuacji?

items.title: RT by @RALee85: Hello everyone. Today I’m starting another fundraiser to get engineering equipment to Ukraine, and I’m asking for your help by sharing, donating, and liking this post. Even if you can’t donate, sharing it genuinely makes a difference. Plase watch the video with their CV90 Crew explaining the importance of this equipment. The donation link is in the comments below. A good friend of mine from the 21st Mechanized Brigade of the UAF has been working on improving the survivability and effectiveness of the 🇸🇪 CV90 IFVs and, most importantly, the soldiers inside them. He recently reached out to me asking for help getting engineering equipment for his brigade. This is one of those things that doesn’t look as dramatic as drones, armored vehicles, or weapons, but it directly saves lives. A properly dug fighting position, trench, vehicle shelter, or reinforced position can be the difference between soldiers surviving an artillery or drone attack and not coming home. Unfortunately, because of bureaucracy and often simple neglect by higher command, excavation equipment remains critically overlooked. It is one of the most obvious low-hanging fruits on the battlefield: relatively inexpensive machinery that can save soldiers’ lives and protect multimillion-dollar equipment. The brigade already has several excavators, but they are in critically bad condition. We are already working on getting those repaired. But even if every one of them were operational, it still wouldn’t be enough for the brigade’s needs. Their full request is for 3 excavators, transportation for them, a crane, and pickup trucks. The total cost would be around $240,000. I wish I could say we can raise all of it, but with the current level of donations, I don’t think that is realistic. So we scaled the fundraiser down to $100,000. That will allow us to purchase 3 excavators and a truck capable of transporting them. It is still a huge amount of money. But these machines will not sit somewhere in storage. They will be working every day, digging positions, protecting vehicles, and giving Ukrainian soldiers a better chance of surviving. And that is why I’m asking for your help. If you can donate, even a small amount helps. If you can’t donate, please like and repost this post. The more people who see it, the better chance we have of reaching this goal. Thank you to everyone who has supported our previous fundraisers and continues supporting Ukraine. Don't mind the snow in the video, they asked for this in march, and unfortunately I couldn't fundraiser until today. But we have been working on repairing their equipment and supplying some machines since June. Donation link is in the 1st comment below.

Ukraine F-16 Pilots Rationing Missiles as Russian Attacks Intensify | NEWSMAX2
Ukraine’s American-made F-16 fighter jets are defending the skies against Russian drones and cruise missiles — but a critical shortage of U.S.-made missiles is putting that mission at risk.
In an exclusive NEWSMAX interview from Kyiv, Ukrainian F-16 wing commander “Phantom” tells foreign correspondent Shelby Wilder that Ukraine needs additional Patriot and AIM-120 missiles, warning that an aircraft without weapons is a “useless tool.”
The shortage has reportedly become so severe that Ukrainian pilots are rationing missiles and, on some missions, relying on their F-16s’ onboard cannons to take down Russian aerial threats.
